Violation ID: 995065
Permit API: 053-29645
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Howe Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/15/2023
Comments: This conventional well is equipped with a pump jack. The well's operator information and API number are displayed on the jack.There is an approximate 1' x 10' area of oil soaked soil on the ground next to the well from repeated venting of this well and its associated discharge of production fluids.A tank battery located 100 feet northeast of this well consists of two 210 bbl stock tanks inside of an earthen diking. There is evidence of production fluid releases onto the gravel inside of the diking given staining of the gravel and elevated specific conductance (SPC) within the stained areas. In addition to the issues inside of the diking, there is upwards of a barrel of crude oil/production fluids outside of the northern diking wall. Two sizable pools of crude oil are present within approximately 25' of the diking, while soil with elevated SPC and an abundance of deer tracks are present across the forest floor for another 25 feet to the north.It is requested that documentation of production water disposal from this lease be provided to the Department. Please see the attached Notice of Violation regarding requested information pertaining to the cause of the release and intentions to remediate the contaminated material within and outside of the tank battery.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation ID: 8168465
Permit API: 129-24616
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Derry Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/12/2023
Comments: On December 12 2023, the Department conducted a follow up inspection of the Keeno 2 OG Well in response to IR 3640044.The findings are as follows: The previosuly observed leaked appeared to be active with fluid observed emanating from the well head in the location of the plunger rod at the time of the inspection. Conductivity readings of the fluid were taken with direct reading of the water of 0.26mS and soil readings of 0.25mS and 0.04mS. Prior to leaving the location, the Department contacted Apollo Resources Representative James Stiffler to inform him of the release. I recommended that the Operator take immediate action to correct the condition creating the release and remediate the area in accordance with the Department's current spill policy. Mr. Stiffler indicated that they would send someone out to correct the leak, by either tightening any loose components or temporarily plugging the place where the leak is occurring from and remediate the area as needed. He also stated that the well is on their list to be plugged. Based on today's inspection, violations remain open for the failure to properly control production fluid and/or other fluids resulting in a release to the ground. The Department has yet to receive clarification as to what caused the release, the quantity of fluid released and how this was determined, and how long it is believed the release was occurring. Please include the clarification information within the NOV response.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to BEECH RESOURCES LLC in Lycoming Township, Lycoming County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/26/2024 to BEECH RESOURCES LLC in Lycoming Township, Lycoming county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BEECH RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/26/2024
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8202739
Permit API: 081-21954
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Lycoming Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/26/2024
Comments: On September 26, 2024, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a routine site inspection at the Beech Resources Delta Well Pad. No E and S issues were observed during the time of inspection. The site appeared to be stable and well vegetated meeting the 70% uniform perennial vegetative cover.Beech Resources contractors were in the process of setting up the well pad with production equipment and working on getting the AST ready for use. During the inspection, the east end of the well pad had some pools of water on it. The DEP screened the pool of water at the northeast corner with a conductivity meter. The conductivity meter measured the conductivity of the pool of water at 6,000 uS/cm. Near the pool of water in the northeast corner was a frack tank outside of containment. This frack tank contained water from the secondary containment of the drilling rig. Adjacent to the frack tank were multiple pallets of hoses used to manifold tanks together. The conductivity of the pool of water near and under the frack tank measured at 13,090 uS/cm. After observing the pools of water with elevated conductivity, the DEP went to the Company Man onsite and informed him of the findings. DEP showed the company where the pool of water was and the Company Man said that Beech Resources Don Stevenson was onsite. After finding Mr. Stevenson, DEP showed where the elevated conductivity pool was. Mr. Stevenson placed a call for a vac truck to mobilize to the well pad to removed the fluid. An excavator was used to dig a sump to collect the fluid so the vac truck could remove the fluid. Once the vac truck arrived onsite, Beech resources began removing the fluid from the sump and around the frack tank. The pallets of hoses were moved onto containment. During the removal of the fluid from the northeast corner conductivity was monitored in the fluid of the sump. Prior to DEP leaving the site, conductivity of the fluid in the sump measured at 3,900 uS/cm. Conductivity of the fluid was higher near the frack tank in the sump that was dug.At 1630 on September 26, 2024, Mr. Stevenson called DEP to inform them that all the fluid had been vacuumed and impacted soil had been removed. Mr. Stevenson said they were able to move the frack tank onto containment. After moving the frack tank, excavation of the impacted soil could begin. Mr. Stevenson said they removed approximately an excavator's bucket width for about 25 feet and removed about 6 inches of soil. Approximately 32 gallons of fluid was vacuumed and two roll off dumpsters were filled with impacted soil.Due to the amount of soil removed combined with the fluid vacuumed up Beech Resources has chosen to remediate to Act 2 standards. Violations of Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.66(b)1, Chapter 78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management Act 301 were noted.

properties.content:

Violation Type: Administrative

Violation ID: 8260076
Permit API: 125-27157
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Independence Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Partial Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/23/2025
Comments: On December 23, 2025, a routine partial inspection was conducted at the Fred Jones well site in Independence Township, Washington County.The Erosion and Sedimentation Control General Permit (ESCGP) was terminated by the Department on January 5, 2017.During this inspection, the Department observed representatives from Precision Pump and Valve Service conducting work on the production tanks. When the Department inquired on the work being conducted during this inspection, the Precision Pump and Valve Service representatives explained that a minor leak was discovered by the operator on December 17, 2025, and they are on site to conduct repairs and maintenance. They also explained that no production fluids were released outside of secondary containment.A disturbed area with temporary stabilization applied was observed on the ground adjacent to the production tanks, however the Precision Pump and Valve Service representatives present were unsure of why this area was disturbed (photos 3 and 4).Based on observations from this inspection, a violation shall be noted and immediately corrected for failure to report tank deficiencies to the Department within 3 days of discovery. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending further investigation.The Department recommends that the accumulated stormwater in the production tank secondary containment is disposed in accordance with current regulations, if it is contaminated with production fluids.The Department requests that the operator provide clarification on why the ground was disturbed adjacent to the production tanks no later than January 9, 2025.

Permit API: 081-21907
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cascade Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/24/2023
Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions at the site after the reported release of produced fluid to the well pad on 3/3/23. The frac is still on-going on the pad. I met with company man Wade Adams upon arriving on location. In the area where the release from 3/3/23 sprayed produced fluid onto the well pad in the south travel lane and southeast of the MASS, puddles of fluid had an electrical conductivity (EC) of 852 uS/cm. Fluid at the outlet of the north stormwater channel had an EC of 478 uS/cm. The well site secondary containment appears to be in good condition. No holes or crushed berms were observed. A vacuum truck was present on the pad which was sucking up fluid from the secondary containment. Violations remain outstanding from the reported release of produced fluid to the pad surface on 3/3/23.

Comments: On February 27, 2025, the Department conducted an inspection on the Hillview Cemetery 2 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. This inspection was conducted to follow up to IR 3872789, where violations were issued against severe rutting observed onsite and for failure to post the API number and operator's information onsite. No response of any kind to IR 3872789 has been received from the operator as of the date of this inspection. NOV response was requested from the operator no later than December 9, 2024.The following was observed:The areas of significant rutting that were previously observed in the access road and well site remain (see photos 1, 2, and 4). The most severely rutted portion in the access road is situated approximately 100 feet from slate Creek, and therefore may continue to pose the potential to threaten the Waters of the Commonwealth (see photo 3). No staining or distressed vegetation was observed on the ground around the well head (see photo 5). The brine tank is disconnected from the well equipment at the time of inspection (see photo 6). No evidence of leaks or distressed vegetation was observed where the disconnected line is located. The brine tank appears to be sound at the time of inspection, with no staining or distressed vegetation on the ground around it (see photos 7 and 8). The API number and a means to identify and/or contact the operator have not been posted onsite since the time of IR 3872789. What appears to be sedimentation was observed immediately downslope of the area of most severe rutting in access road (see photo 9). It does not appear to have reached the Waters of the Commonwealth.Based on observations from this inspection, violations issued under IR 3872789 shall remain outstanding, as it appears that no corrective action has been taken onsite since IR 3872789 was conducted.The Department recommends that the brine tank is removed from site if it is no longer in use for production, in accordance with OGA3216(C).

properties.content:
Report Details

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 966153
Permit API: 081-21882
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/25/2022
Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess overall site conditions after multiple spills occurred on Pad B since fracing began on the pad early in the year. I met with EQT company man Justin Hamill upon arriving on Pad B. Nine wells have been drilled on Pad B but not all of the wells have been completed. Equipment from the frac has been removed from the pad. Most of the well site secondary containment has been removed from the pad. The secondary containment remains in the southeast area of the pad. The southeast corner of the containment was pulled back somewhat during this inspection and revealed fluid with electrical conductivity (EC) from 4.32 to 3.10 mS/cm which had been beneath the containment. A puddle with an EC of 3.00 mS/cm was also observed on the pad surface south of the sump installed in the north stormwater channel. The EC of the fluid in the sump was 1.4 mS/cm. The stormwater channel appeared dry.On Pad A, six wells are staged for production. Six GPUs are present within secondary containment. The GPUs and containment appear to be in good condition. A battery of frac tanks is present within secondary containment. The tanks and containment appear to be in good condition. Violations remain outstanding.

Violation ID: 992558
Permit API: 015-23753
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Terry Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 4/26/2023
Comments: On 4/26/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an Administrative inspection on the Chesapeake Grippo well site. This inspection is to report the results of one water sample that was collected from a 60' x 60' water/ice puddle that was located southeast of the well heads and adjacent to the south edge of secondary containment for six frac tanks.During an inspection on 3/30/2023, the department discovered elevated conductance fluid on the well pad surface outside of containment. The fluid covered a 60' x 60' area and field tested at 4.05 mS conductance with an Oakton PCTS-50 meter. The department collected water sample #9551-049 for laboratory analysis from location Lat: 41.64109 Long: -76.35054. On 4/20/2023 the department received the results of the laboratory analysis that shows elevated barium, strontium, lithium and chlorides and is indicative of brine/production fluid being released onto the pad. The sample report is displayed in pictures 5 and 6. Chesapeake is pursuing Act 2 for the site in response to that incident.The release of fluid with elevated conductance to the pad surface during production operations constitutes violations of SWMA 301, CSL 402, 25 PA Code 78a.57(a) and 78a.66(b)(2).Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3529982 for elevated conductance fluid being discovered on the unprotected pad surface and for inspection ID 3517519 for high conductance fluid discovered on the unprotected pad surface after fracking operations and for elevated conductance fluid discovered on the unprotected pad surface during drilling operations.

Inspection Date: 3/16/2023
Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72-hr (Stepped) pressure build-up tests, (SPBUT) being performed on all (7) wells on the Susan pad. The Susan 2H, 4H and the 5H are older wells and the 24HC, 25HC, 125HC and the 126HC were recently completed. These tests are being performed to assess the results of the initial remedial deployment of Renegades localized casing expansion tool in the production casing of the Susan 4H and 5H completed on 5/26/2021. This is the fourth testing since initial remedial work was performed. SPBUTs were initiated on 3/13/23 @ ~ 12:25 and progressed by shutting in the outer most annuli of each well for first 24-hrs, then in 24-hr progressions, sequentially shutting in the next inner annuli, resulting in a total 72-hr SPBUT. - All (7) wells annuli are shut in. - Upon arrival I met with CALLC Field Rep. Dalton Johnson and Creston Consultant Rep. Jason Rajan. Starting at approx. 12:25pm, ending annuli pressures were checked using a Digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Rep., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter. Creston Consultant collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis. CALLC will share gas sample results with The Department when received. The plan should also include a schedule for heightened annular monitoring of these wells and a mechanical integrity assessment performed by a licensed engineer. Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/14/2026
Comments: This inspection was conducted to evaluate the status of violations issued on 9/18/2025 and 4/17/2026 associated with the construction of the well site for this proposed conventional well and the access road leading to it. Since the 4/17/2026 inspection, Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) submitted multiple versions of an updated E and S plan that included additional BMPs and methods to stabilize all disturbed areas. At the time of this inspection, the latest version of the updated E and S plan has not yet met the expectations of the Department's Technical Services staff, as was indicated in a 5/11/2026 email to William Cenk.Throughout this inspection, we observed that a majority of the practices prescribed in the latest version of the updated E and S plan have been implemented. Inlet/outlet rock protection was placed at the installed culverts, rock filters placed in the roadside ditch in the vicinity of the well site for proposed Well # 3, and a combination of erosion blankets and mulch was applied to temporarily stabilize most of the disturbed areas. TMP indicated that seed was applied prior to mulching/placement of the erosion blanket. Erosion blanket was missing upslope of Culvert 1 and there was no evidence of hydro-seeding. The placement of grubbing material along the southern side of the access road that has displaced stream flow continues to result in accelerated erosion and washout along the southern edge of the road and perimeter of the well site for proposed Well # 4.The Department suggests the removal of the stockpile material from approximately the outlet location of Culvert 3 westerly to the newly established point of concentrated flow. Currently, it appears the streamflow is obstructed and migrated towards the pad/access road creating concentrated flow which cannot be stabilized. Without proper stabilization, the additional flow due to the construction activity appears to be causing accelerated erosion and sedimentation to Wetland G. The removal of the waste areas would potentially allow the flow to migrate back to its original drainage path and allow for successful installation of temporary stabilization BMPs, per plan. Department staff can be available for consultation/direction during the removal operation. Waste areas are not to be discarded in other floodways or wetlands. After the submission of the updated and complete E and S plan to Brian Ayers (brayers@pa.gov), temporary stabilization shall be finished. A follow up inspection will be conducted following the completion of the temporary stabilization. A preapplication meeting must be submitted/scheduled before June 15, 2026 in order to address any outstanding violations.Violations that were cited in the 9/18/2025 and 4/17/2026 inspection reports remain unaddressed.The following were in attendance for this inspection:DEP - Aquatic Biologist Samantha Lutz, Aquatic Biologist Jessica McDuff and WQSS Brian Ayers.Trinity Mineral Partners - Kyle Miller, Brian Bennett and Todd Fantaskey (Northwest Soil Services)

Comments: On March 16, 2026, the Department conducted an incident inspection at the Ziolkowoski Well Site (NOT approved on 11/6/2023) in regard to a release reported to the Department on 3/15/2026 (CTS 395839). Present during the inspection was operator representative Nick Reda.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspections, the Act 9 sign was present and appeared to be properly installed in accordance with 78a55. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan (which contained all required components) and site plans were present in the onsite mailbox.At the time of inspection, there are 14 total wells on the well pad. Wells (2H, 3H, 4H, 5H, 6H, 7H, 8H, 9H, 1H,10H,11H,12H, and 14H) appeared equipped for production with well tags present. Mr. Reda stated they are currently swapping out equipment to complete flowback operations on the 13H.Upon inspection, all necessary drilling equipment appeared to be within secondary containment. The secondary containment appeared to be installed correctly with no tears or leaks. No fluid leaks or spills were identified around any of the well heads or cellars. The production tanks and GPUs appeared to be within secondary containment and appeared sound with no visible fluid leaks.During the inspection, Mr. Reda guided the Department to the location(s) of the reported release. According to Mr. Reda the release occurred on 3/15/2026. He stated the release was caused by a scrubber malfunction on a third-party water truck. At the time of the inspection the operator is estimating a total release of 15 gallons of produced water released to the graveled access road.The Department observed the location(s) of the release and remediation. It appeared the area of the release was split into two different sections of the access road. Mr. Reda said due to the malfunction of the scrubber on the water truck, the release occurred only on the steep portions of the access road. Therefore, the release began approximately halfway down the access road, ceased as the truck reached a level area, and then continued to release on another steep section towards the bottom of the access road.Upon inspection of where the release began, the Department observed an area where impacted material was excavated from the access road (photos 12-13). According to Mr. Reda, the release in this area of the access road was about 150 feet in length and about 1 foot in width. Small puddles of rainwater were observed in this section of the access road. Conductivity readings of 0.49mS, 0.24mS, and 0.43mS, were obtained in the area of the release/remediation. These readings appeared comparable to the background conductivity reading of 0.60mS obtained in the gravel on the side of the access road near the well pad entrance (away from the spill and heavy vehicle traffic). Prior to leaving the site, the area of excavation was backfilled with clean gravel (Photos 23-24).Upon inspection of where the release continued near the bottom of the access road, the Department observed fresh gravel (Photo 17). Mr. Reda stated the impacted material had been removed and the area of excavation had been backfilled. Mr. Reda stated the release in the area of the access road was about 180 feet in length and about 1 foot in width. Conductivity readings of 0.12mS, 0.15mS, and 0.23mS were obtained in the area of the release/remediation. These readings appeared comparable to the background conductivity reading of 0.60mS obtained.Mr. Reda stated all impacted material was placed into 3 roll-off boxes (photos 21-22) and would be disposed of properly. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued as immediately corrected for the observed release as it appeared to be remediated in accordance with current regulations (78a66).

Comments: On January 6, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an administrative inspection for a spill at the Inflection Energy Hensler Well Pad. On January 5, 2022, around 2140, Zac Subra reported a spill of approximately 30 gallons of hydraulic fluid to the well pad surface. At about 920 on January 6, 2022, DEP spoke with Zac Subra on the phone. Mr. Subra said a hydraulic fluid line on a water truck ruptured and caused the spill. Inflection contractors began removing the hydraulic fluid and excavating the impacted soil immediately. Inflection contractors excavated an area of about 20 ft. X 15 ft. of the pad surface. Due to the ground being frozen, Inflection contractors only had to scrape the top of the pad surface to remove the impacted soil in the previously noted area. The impacted soil was added to a rolloff dumpster and hauled to a landfill. Inflection then went back to the pad during the day to verify that the impacted soil had been completely removed. Zac said a small amount of remaining soil had to be removed at this time since it was not observed earlier in the morning. The small amount of soil was added to barrels and is awaiting approval to be disposed of. Inflection then backfilled the excavated area with clean fill. Photos of the area excavated and clean up were provided by Inflection Energy. The spill of hydraulic fluid outside of containment is a violation of Clean Streams Law Section 402(b), Solid Waste Management Act Section 301, and Chapter 78a.54. The violations have been immediately corrected.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/30/2023 to EQT ARO LLC in Plunketts Creek Township, Lycoming county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/30/2023
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 1000298
Permit API: 081-21944
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Plunketts Creek Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/30/2023
Comments: A routine inspection was conducted in order to assess overall site conditions. A Precision Drilling rig is still in operation on the well pad. I first looked at the trench along the side of the well site secondary containment. The electrical conductivity of the fluid in the trench was 764 uS/cm. A sheen was observed on the surface near the ramp over for the backyard area which appeared consistent with an iron-reducing bacteria sheen. Company man Pat Smith walked over to me while I was looking at the trench and told me that there had just been a release of a base oil to the pad surface next to the upright base oil tanks. We walked over to the base oil tanks and I saw an area of fluid on the pad surface immediately adjacent to the secondary containment for the base oil tanks. The area was approximately 30 ft by 10 ft. Mr. Smith said that the estimated volume of the release was 20 gallons. The electrical conductivity of the fluid was 1.0 uS/cm as measured by the Oakton conductivity meter. Mr. Smith said that Tobias Excavation was on the way to scrape up the impacted pad material. On July 2, 2023 EQT representative Rick Hall sent an email to the Department which included a document which detailed the remediation of the base oil release. The report included the volume of material excavated, 8 tons, the dimensions of the pad that was scraped, 20 ft wide by 40 ft long by 6 ft deep, as well as photos of the area during excavation and after the area was backfilled with new gravel. Violations noted and considered immediately corrected.

Permit API: 083-46720
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/07/2026
Comments: I conducted a follow up inspection of this conventional well that had a release occur in November of 2025, when a steel gathering line had ruptured resulting in crude oil contaminating ditches and soil. Initially the remediation of the site was progressing. There had been no signs of product at the under flow dams, there was no viable oil in the ditches. In preperation of obtaining confirmatory soil samples to evaluate if the remediation was sufficient, it was discovered another leak had developed on a different section of the same line. This operator indicated they will replace all of the steel line for this well with plastic/poly line. This release was caught early and as of now, appears to be less than 1 bbl of lost product and has impacted a minimal amount of soil.Bull Run employees had a roll off dumpster en-route to remove the impacted soil. The ruptured line was sucked out with a vac truck and will be removed while running new poly line. Further inspections will be conducted to document ongoing remedation efforts, as well as confirmatory sampling to show that the remediation is sufficient.

Comments On 9/28/2016, I performed an inspection of Range Resources Robert Hamilton well site. Present at time of inspection was Nick Reda and Brandon Carson (Range Resources). Representatives from Equipment Transport where present completing remediation of the spill. The site is located in West Finley Twp., Washington County. The inspection was performed as a response to a reported diesel spill by the operator. The operator reported a spill of a diesel fuel to the Hamilton Well Pad. It is estimated that approximately 60-70 gallons of diesel was released to the graveled pad during loading of produced water, after the water truck experienced an engine runaway. The runaway broke the truck’s driveshaft which in turn punctured the fuel tank, resulting in the fuel release. Liquids from the truck’s tank were transferred via another water truck, and the damaged truck was removed. Absorbent pads were deployed immediately following the release, and remediation of the affected gravel / soil was initiated once the truck was moved. The operator was in process of removing impacted material which was being stored in sealed roll-off boxes on site for disposal. Three boxes where noted filled on site and more where being delivered to the site. The operator intends to follow the Department’s guidance for Alternative Remediation for this release.
